problem: Add a non-null boolean column is_archived with default false to the orders table in production
context: PostgreSQL 15. The orders table has 50 million rows and takes steady write traffic. Migrations run through our standard migration tool in a single transaction.
key_facts: Since PostgreSQL 11, ADD COLUMN with a constant default is a metadata-only change: it does not rewrite the table and holds its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock only briefly.
constraints: The orders table must stay writable throughout; no multi-minute locks

options.summary: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN is_archived boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false in one migration
Add the column as nullable, backfill false in batches of 10k rows, then add a NOT NULL constraint with NOT VALID and validate it separately
Create orders_v2 with the new column, dual-write from the app, copy historical rows, then swap tables

criteria.description: Low risk of locking or downtime on a large, busy table
Few steps and little code to write and operate

expected.why: Constant defaults are metadata-only since PG 11; the elaborate options add risk and work for nothing.
